limits: Python and libraries on this page: the examples run in your browser, in Python 3.13.2 with xmltodict 1.0.4, defusedxml 0.7.1 and openpyxl 3.1.5 (the versions the research ran, embedded as wheels) on Pyodide's own lxml 6.0.0, while the research ran Python 3.14.6 with lxml 6.1.3. Each concept example and each chapter example was run in the browser and compared with its recorded result.

Recorded, not run: two examples need something a browser cannot give and show the output recorded under Python 3.14.6, labelled so: DefaultEncodingIsLocale, SerializationErrorNotes. The first starts other Python programs with other locale settings; the second shows the notes that Python 3.14 adds to a JSON error, which Python 3.13 does not have.

The four libraries: defusedxml-0.7.1-py2.py3-none-any.whl, et_xmlfile-2.0.0-py3-none-any.whl, openpyxl-3.1.5-py2.py3-none-any.whl, xmltodict-1.0.4-py3-none-any.whl are embedded as the PyPI wheels, unchanged, and unpacked in the browser; their licences are MIT, PSFL (recorded in 03-materials/ch18/assets/ASSETS_PROVENANCE_v1_0_0.md). No file of the book's online materials (a zip of 7,759,877 bytes) is on this page: every example builds its own CSV, JSON and XML text in memory or in a temporary folder.

NOT EXECUTED: Microsoft Excel itself (LibreOffice 24.2 stood in for it), a Windows computer (the translation of line ends that Windows text mode does was reproduced by asking io.TextIOWrapper for it), Python 3.14.7 and 3.14.8 and the final Python 3.15.0 (uv offered only 3.15.0b4), the language model clean-up of the chapter, and the Practice Program as readers would write it (a converter was written to the printed skeleton and run on the shipped workbooks). Wherever a page of this site shows a line ending translated as Windows does it, that is EMULATED with io.TextIOWrapper, and says so.

MEASURED, single runs on the machine of the day, not results of a program on this page: peak memory: list(reader) 69.0 MiB, loop 0.166 MiB (ratio 416) | time: list 0.90 s, loop 0.40 s, DictReader loop 1.22 s; ElementTree parse (whole tree)       peak   108.3 MiB  1.22 s; minidom (DOM, whole tree)            peak   440.6 MiB  7.33 s; SAX (stream)                         peak     0.4 MiB  1.55 s; seconds 0.12 (billion laughs, ElementTree).

What the public sites answered on 2026-10-12 is in live_observations_v1_0_0.json: the chapter's page (status 200, 83,216 bytes, equal to the digest in the book's ontology), the newest PyPI releases (xmltodict 1.0.4, openpyxl 3.1.5, defusedxml 0.7.1) and the pages of the stories.

One program was run under 11 interpreters (3.11.17, 3.12.3, 3.13.16, 3.14.0, 3.14.1, 3.14.2, 3.14.3, 3.14.4, 3.14.5, 3.14.6, 3.15.0b4) with the same package versions; the 11 items that differ between them are listed in interpreter_record_v1_0_0.json (for example the quoting constants of 3.11, the message of an empty quotechar in 3.14, the notes on a JSON error in 3.14). The book's Appendix A pins xmltodict 0.13.0 and openpyxl 3.1.5, and the chapter's statements were also replayed with those versions.
